checkpoints: Async streaming replication lets the primary commit and acknowledge a write before the replica has replayed the corresponding WAL, leaving a window where the replica's replay position trails the primary's sent position.

Both halves of the code are individually correct: routing the write through createQueryRunner("master") correctly updates the primary, and routing the reload through createQueryRunner("slave") correctly targets the replica; the stale read only surfaces once the two calls are composed back-to-back.

An immediate reload issued right after a write can land inside the replication lag window, before the just-written WAL has been applied on the replica, so the replica is correctly returning the pre-write row rather than malfunctioning.
The lag is a measurable, observable quantity, not a guess: pg_wal_lsn_diff(sent_lsn, replay_lsn) > 0 on the primary shows how far behind the replica currently is at any moment.

The targeted fix is read-your-writes consistency: route only the post-write reload for this specific operation through createQueryRunner("master") — or return the value already held in memory from the write instead of re-querying at all — rather than forcing every read in the app back onto the primary.

Every other read path, such as findAll() and general list/detail queries, should stay routed through createQueryRunner("slave"); scoping the fix narrowly to the read-after-write case preserves the scaling benefit the primary/replica split exists for.

The stale reload is an instance of eventual consistency, the accepted trade-off for offloading reads to a replica, so the correct response is to special-case the sensitive read-after-write path rather than dismantle the read/write split entirely.

The fix can be verified by artificially growing replication lag — for example pausing or throttling the replica so replication_lag_bytes increases — to reproduce the stale read on the original slave-routed reload, then confirming the primary-routed reload stays fresh even while the replica continues to lag.
